span.label: **THE PRIME WORKS LEAST ON THE PEOPLE IT IS ABOUT, AND THIS IS PREDICTED IN ADVANCE RATHER THAN EXPLAINED AFTERWARDS:** `Quotation withheld.` higgins1977 raises exactly this variable in ONE CONJECTURAL SENTENCE - `There may even be individual differences in the relative accessibility of different categories` - and does not test it. **This paper builds four studies on it and finds it REVERSES the priming effect**, so the same trait that makes someone morally consistent is the one that makes them unprimeable. A 1977 aside and its test 32 years later, both in this corpus. (The term `chronic accessibility` is Higgins, King & Mavin 1982 and appears nowhere in higgins1977.) A study sampling only committed people would find nothing and conclude the effect is not real
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **PRIMING PLACED AS ONE ROUTE AMONG THREE TO THE SAME STATE:** `Quotation withheld, to REPEATED ACTS OF self-definition (Higgins, 1989).` Three roads to accessibility, of which the experimental one is only the fastest. **That sentence does more for a corpus about priming than most results do, because it says what priming is an INSTANCE OF** - and it makes the individual-difference moderator in this paper a consequence of the theory rather than a nuisance variable. (The quote stops before `self-definition`, which the staged text renders as a hyphen-loss fusion.)
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND STUDY 4 REVERSES THE MODERATION OVER TIME, WHICH A ONE-SHOT STUDY WOULD HAVE SCORED AS A NULL:** initially the prime does little for high-centrality people, exactly as the ceiling account predicts. But under repeated feedback that others are behaving selfishly, `Quotation withheld.` **The prime's value is not the initial push but the resistance to decay.** A corpus that records only peak effect sizes cannot represent this finding at all
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **THE MODERATION IS STATED TWICE AND THE SECOND TIME IT IS A RESULT:** `Quotation withheld.` The mechanism is a headroom argument, and it is testable: it predicts that any manipulation raising a construct's accessibility will show the same inverse relation to that construct's chronic strength. **This record and higgins1977 are the two ends of that claim in this corpus, and the two ends are not equal** - higgins1977 says only `THERE MAY EVEN BE individual differences in the relative accessibility of different categories`, a speculation with no test attached, while this paper makes that variable its moderator and predicts where a prime will fail
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: moral prime —causes→ current accessibility
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — **`INTERACTIVE INFLUENCE` IS IN THE QUOTE AND IS THE PART THIS EDGE CANNOT CARRY.** The measured relation is not `prime raises accessibility` but `prime raises accessibility MORE for people low in moral identity centrality, and barely at all for people high in it`. `increases` is true on average and is what the study found; a reader who stops there has the paper's headline and not its result. The moderation is quoted whole in the first and fourth senses. Weight 0.9 - four studies, and the mediation is formally tested by Muller et al.'s procedure rather than asserted.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: current accessibility —causes→ moral action
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE SECOND LEG OF THE MEDIATION, and together with the edge above it is the paper's model written as a path: situation -> current accessibility -> moral action. `LINKS` is the paper's own verb and it is doing mediation work - this is the summary sentence for Studies 1 and 2 in the general discussion, not a hypothesis. Weight 0.9.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: moral identity centrality —causes→ current accessibility
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.85 — **THE TRAIT LEG, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MAKES THE PAPER'S RESULT COUNTERINTUITIVE.** Centrality raises chronic accessibility - which is why the PRIME does less for people high in it. So this edge and the `moral prime -> current accessibility` edge point at the same target for opposite reasons, and the graph shows two arrows where the paper has a ceiling. **`moderates` is not in the enforced vocabulary (Q-804)**, so nothing here records that the second edge shrinks as the first grows. Weight 0.85 rather than 0.9: this leg is theory plus the Study 1 mediation test, where the prime leg is directly manipulated.
